neurips-2022-metateacher-coordinating-mu.tldr: MetaTeacher coordinates multiple pretrained source models to learn from limited target-domain labels.
paragraphs: Medical-image adaptation may involve a small labeled target dataset, many unlabeled target examples, and several models trained on related source domains. This combines semisupervised learning with adaptation that does not revisit source data. MetaTeacher addresses the difficulty of making those ingredients work together.

The framework learns how to coordinate adaptation of individual source models, passes feedback between source and target models, and uses semisupervised bilevel optimization to organize their updates. The aim is to exploit complementary source knowledge without assuming every pretrained model is equally useful for the target setting.

Experiments across five chest X-ray datasets outperform the compared state-of-the-art alternatives. The abstract does not report numerical classification gains or clinical deployment outcomes. The contribution is a coordinated learning framework for this particular combination of limited supervision and multiple available source models, supported by image-classification evaluations rather than evidence of general diagnostic superiority.

neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.tldr: IISE chooses between cheap biased simulators and expensive accurate evaluations to identify the best option.
paragraphs: A decision-maker may have several simulators for each option, with different costs and accuracy. Multi-fidelity best-arm identification asks which option is best while minimizing the total cost of the evaluations needed to reach a high-confidence conclusion.

The authors derive a lower bound assuming known maximum bias for each fidelity. Their Iterative Imprecise Successive Elimination algorithm, IISE, chooses among fidelities and has a cost upper bound reflecting the structure of that lower bound. It provably improves on methods that ignore the available fidelity structure.

More detailed knowledge of approximation errors can further reduce the algorithm’s cost. Numerical experiments in simulated domains validate the benefits. The guarantees depend on the learner’s information about simulator bias; they do not justify treating arbitrary cheap approximations as reliable. The work formalizes how uncertainty and evaluation price can jointly govern sequential experimental decisions.

neurips-2022-planning-for-sample-efficie.tldr: EfficientImitate combines planning, behavioral cloning, and adversarial imitation to reduce environment interactions.
paragraphs: Behavioral cloning learns without new environment interactions but can suffer when its actions lead away from demonstration states. Adversarial imitation can improve behavior through distribution matching, yet often needs many interactions. EfficientImitate aims to combine strong performance with a smaller interaction budget.

The framework extends adversarial imitation to reinforcement learning based on Monte Carlo tree search and unifies it with behavioral cloning. Planning provides the common structure through which the two imitation approaches can contribute their respective advantages.

On state-based and image-based DeepMind Control tasks, the authors report state-of-the-art performance and sample efficiency. In limited-sample settings, performance improves by over 4x, and the method solves challenging tasks such as Humanoid where earlier methods fail with few interactions. The abstract does not give the precise interaction budgets or define every reported aggregate, so the gains remain specific to the evaluated settings.

neurips-2022-prospect-labeled-tandem-mas.tldr: PROSPECT supplies labeled proteomics data and evaluation guidance for peptide-prediction tasks.
paragraphs: Bottom-up proteomics digests proteins into peptides and analyzes them using tandem mass spectrometry. Machine-learning models can help predict peptide properties and improve identification, but comparing methods requires common data and evaluation conventions. This paper introduces PROSPECT as a labeled reference dataset spanning multiple proteomics tasks.

The work focuses on peptide retention-time prediction and tandem mass-spectrum prediction. Alongside the data, the authors review existing approaches and task formulations from a machine-learning perspective and recommend evaluation metrics and visualizations.

The intended benefit is more reproducible comparison and better assessment of generalization, while making the area accessible to machine-learning researchers. The abstract does not provide the dataset’s sample count or a new model’s numerical performance. Its contribution is primarily an evaluation resource and methodological guidance, rather than a claim that a particular predictor has already solved peptide characterization or demonstrated clinical utility.

neurips-2022-reconstructing-training-dat.tldr: Some trained neural classifiers expose substantial portions of their training data through their parameters.
paragraphs: Neural networks may retain information about individual training examples, raising questions about both learning behavior and privacy. This paper asks whether actual examples can be reconstructed directly from the parameters of a trained classifier, beyond merely determining whether a sample was used.

The authors develop a reconstruction scheme motivated by theoretical results about the implicit bias of gradient-based neural-network training. The reported result is that, in some cases, a significant fraction of the training data can be recovered from the fitted model.

Demonstrations use binary multilayer-perceptron classifiers on several standard computer-vision datasets. The abstract does not quantify the recovered fraction or establish the same vulnerability for every architecture and training procedure. Its privacy implication is concrete but scoped: releasing a trained model can expose more than aggregate patterns, and the demonstrated reconstruction attacks warrant attention to the particular training and model conditions.

neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.tldr: External image retrieval lets smaller generative models reuse content and adapt by changing the database.
paragraphs: Image generators often grow by storing more training information in larger parameter sets. This paper explores a semiparametric alternative: pair a comparatively small diffusion or autoregressive model with an external image database and a retrieval mechanism.

During training, nearest neighbors from that database condition the generator. Retrieved examples provide local content while the model learns how to compose scenes. Experiments show that replacing the database after training can transfer the generator to a new domain without retraining its parameters.

The approach performs competitively on tasks not explicitly used for training, including class-conditional generation, zero-shot stylization, and text-to-image generation without paired text-image training data. The authors report reduced parameter counts and state-of-the-art improvements with negligible retrieval overhead in their setup. The abstract gives no numerical costs, so those efficiency claims should remain tied to the evaluated systems.

neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.tldr: Social-Inverse learns to solve a social-contagion task from decisions made for another task.
paragraphs: When an underlying system is complex or only partly known, examples of good decisions may be more accessible than its full model. This paper formalizes inverse decision-making with task migration: using query-decision pairs from task A to solve a different task B.

The authors develop a general framework for social-contagion management, where decisions depend on a latent stochastic process. A generalization analysis supports the learning approach, asking when experience from one type of decision can inform another without first observing the complete decision-making system.

Empirical studies include a sanity check and comparisons with learning-based and graph-based alternatives. The reported results are promising and support the feasibility of cross-task decision transfer in the studied setting. The abstract does not provide metrics or exact migration assumptions, so it does not establish that arbitrary pairs of decision problems can be solved from one another’s examples.

neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.tldr: Branched transport combines efficient geometry optimization with approximate search over network topology.
paragraphs: Branched optimal transport favors shared routes because shipping additional mass along an existing edge has subadditive cost. This produces network structures resembling branching delivery systems. The paper studies the NP-hard problem of connecting finitely many sources and sinks in the Euclidean plane.

For a fixed network topology, the authors show how to efficiently find its best geometry. They also argue that an optimal topology never needs more than three edges meeting at one branching point. These structural results extend to transportation networks on two-dimensional Riemannian manifolds.

The proposed approximate solver combines geometric optimization with combinatorial topology search. The abstract describes it as simple and effective but supplies no numerical evaluation or global approximation factor. The work distinguishes an efficiently solvable geometric subproblem from the harder choice of connectivity, using theoretical structure to guide a practical approach to the combined optimization.

neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.tldr: Theory quantifies how exact or approximate symmetry affects a model’s approximation and generalization tradeoff.
paragraphs: Equivariant models build known symmetries into their architecture, often with the expectation of better generalization. Real data may obey those symmetries only approximately, creating a tension between imposing useful structure and restricting the model too strongly. This paper investigates that tradeoff formally.

The authors derive quantitative generalization bounds for models that capture task-specific symmetries. They then compare approximate equivariance in the model with approximate equivariance in the data distribution, connecting the two types of error for a given symmetry group.

The analysis identifies conditions under which a particular amount of model-equivariance error is optimal for the task and data. The abstract does not provide empirical benchmarks or claim that stronger symmetry is always better. Its contribution is a unified theoretical account of when symmetry helps and how imperfect symmetry changes the choice of an appropriate model constraint.

neurips-2023-artic3d-learning-robust-art.tldr: ARTIC3D uses skeleton-based geometry and diffusion guidance to reconstruct articulated shapes from noisy images.
paragraphs: Reconstructing articulated animals from sparse web images is difficult because viewpoint, pose, lighting, occlusion, and truncation are entangled. ARTIC3D is a self-supervised framework that represents shapes with a skeleton-based surface and uses Stable Diffusion’s two-dimensional priors to guide reconstruction.

The method first enhances incomplete images to obtain cleaner masks and semantic features. Diffusion-guided optimization then estimates shape and texture, using a proposed technique for more stable image-level gradients. A final refinement under rigid-part transformations supports animation of the reconstructed model.

Evaluations cover existing datasets and newly introduced noisy web-image collections. The reported outputs are more robust to damaged observations, richer in shape and texture detail, and more realistic when animated. The abstract does not give quantitative scores or guarantee recovery of hidden true geometry; its claims concern improved reconstructions and animations under the evaluated visual conditions.

neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.tldr: Tempered exponential measures generalize AdaBoost and create a tunable family of boosting losses.
paragraphs: AdaBoost can be derived from relative-entropy minimization with normalized positive example weights. This paper replaces that setup with tempered exponential measures, which normalize a specified power of the measure and introduce a parameter t controlling the generalization.

The resulting t-AdaBoost recovers ordinary AdaBoost at t = 1. For t in [0, 1), the authors retain exponential convergence and slightly improve its hidden constant while guaranteeing bounded leveraging coefficients. The construction partly uses a generalized arithmetic associated with the tempered measures.

The corresponding objective yields a family of tempered losses for domain-partitioning classifiers such as decision trees. These losses are strictly proper and span the known range of boosting rates. Experiments with boosted trees show that tuning t can produce substantial benefits. The abstract gives no benchmark scores, so the empirical takeaway is tunability rather than one universally optimal parameter value.

neurips-2023-cbd-a-certified-backdoor-de.tldr: CBD supplies backdoor-detection decisions together with conditional certificates and false-positive bounds.
paragraphs: Backdoored classifiers behave normally on ordinary inputs but respond incorrectly to a trigger. CBD introduces a detector based on local dominant probability and an adjustable conformal-prediction scheme. It provides a detection decision, conditions guaranteeing detectability, and a probabilistic upper bound on false positives.

The theory links stronger guarantees to triggers that tolerate test-time noise and use smaller perturbations. Experiments cover four datasets and several attack types. For random perturbation triggers with l2 magnitude at most 0.75 and attack success above 90%, empirical and certified detection rates are reported separately.

Those empirical/certified rates are 100%/98% on GTSRB, 100%/84% on SVHN, 98%/98% on CIFAR-10, and 72%/40% on TinyImageNet, with low false-positive rates. The certification is conditional on the stated framework and attack properties; it is not a guarantee of detecting every possible backdoor.

neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.tldr: CoDA jointly discovers novel 3D boxes and aligns their features with images and text.
paragraphs: Open-vocabulary three-dimensional detection must both locate unfamiliar objects and assign categories beyond a limited annotated base set. CoDA addresses these tasks together, using complementary geometric and semantic information rather than assuming novel object boxes are already available.

Its discovery step combines three-dimensional box priors with two-dimensional open-vocabulary semantics to create pseudo box labels. Cross-modal alignment then connects point-cloud features with image and text features through class-agnostic and class-discriminative objectives. Newly discovered objects enter this alignment process, and better alignment in turn improves localization.

Experiments on SUN-RGBD and ScanNet report an 80% improvement in mean average precision over the strongest alternative. The abstract states a relative improvement, not an 80-percentage-point gain. It provides no absolute scores. The contribution is the mutually reinforcing discovery-and-alignment framework, with evidence on these two three-dimensional scene benchmarks.

neurips-2023-counterfactual-generation-w.tldr: MATTE identifies dependent content and style factors under structural assumptions for unsupervised style transfer.
paragraphs: Counterfactual generation often requires separating latent content from style, but those factors may be dependent. Their relationship can also change across domains, such as different positive words appearing in food and movie reviews. This paper addresses that dependency instead of assuming independent latent factors.

The authors derive identifiability guarantees by exploiting relative sparsity in the influences of different latent variables. Those insights lead to MATTE, a domain-adaptive counterfactual-generation model designed to handle domain-varying content-style dependence.

On four large-scale datasets, MATTE achieves state-of-the-art unsupervised style-transfer results without paired examples or style labels. The abstract does not spell out all identifiability conditions or provide performance scores. The guarantees therefore depend on the stated structural framework, rather than implying that arbitrary unlabeled data uniquely reveal their causal factors or that every generated change is a valid real-world counterfactual.

neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.tldr: Perturbed spanning forests make clustering differentiable within end-to-end learning pipelines.
paragraphs: Clustering typically makes discrete grouping decisions, which can complicate learning through the clustering operation as part of a larger model. This paper introduces a differentiable construction based on stochastic perturbations of minimum-weight spanning forests.

The method permits efficient gradients through the resulting clustering step, making it usable inside end-to-end trainable pipelines. The authors also design a dedicated loss for learning from partial clustering information, allowing supervision that does not fully specify every grouping decision.

Experiments cover supervised and semisupervised tasks across several datasets, including noisy data and difficult geometries. The abstract reports good performance but does not identify benchmarks, quantify gains, or specify a universal recovery condition. The contribution is a concrete bridge between discrete forest-based clustering and gradient-based learning, supported by demonstrations that the operation remains useful beyond simple, clean cluster shapes.

neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.tldr: ALIA uses language-guided image editing and filtering to diversify fine-grained training datasets.
paragraphs: Fine-grained classifiers trained on small datasets may fail when context changes, such as weather or location. ALIA, Automated Language-guided Image Augmentation, uses large vision and language models to describe the domains present in a dataset and create useful visual variations.

The generated descriptions guide image editing. A model trained on the original data filters edits that are too minor or that corrupt class-relevant information, aiming to retain recognizable examples while increasing contextual diversity. This filtering is an explicit part of the augmentation pipeline.

On fine-grained classification tasks, including domain-generalization and contextual-bias settings, ALIA outperforms traditional augmentation and data generated directly from text prompts. The abstract provides no numerical improvements or error rate for the filter. The evidence supports the complete generation-and-filtering procedure, rather than the assumption that every diffusion-generated edit preserves a valid training label.

neurips-2023-django-detecting-trojans-in.tldr: Django weights vulnerable object boxes to improve backdoor-trigger inversion for detection models.
paragraphs: Backdoor detectors often try to reverse-engineer a trigger, but object detectors produce many bounding-box predictions with different vulnerability to the same trigger. Treating all boxes equally can misalign the inversion objective. Django addresses that detection-specific problem.

The framework dynamically applies Gaussian weights to emphasize more vulnerable victim boxes and calibrate their contributions during trigger inversion. A label-proposal preprocessing step further improves efficiency. The method is evaluated as a detector of compromised models, rather than as a procedure for removing their backdoors.

Experiments span three image datasets, three architectures, two attack types, and 168 models. Django outperforms six state-of-the-art baselines, with improvements of up to 38% in accuracy and a 10x reduction in overhead. These are maximum reported gains in the evaluated settings; the abstract does not establish equivalent benefits against arbitrary unseen attack strategies.

neurips-2023-first-order-stochastic-opti.tldr: List-decodable stochastic optimization tolerates independent corruption without bounded moments or zero mean.
paragraphs: This paper studies stochastic gradients containing ordinary bounded-variance observation noise plus independent oblivious noise. The additional corruption need not be centered or have bounded moments. Its central restriction is that it equals zero with probability at least alpha and is independent of both the query point and observation noise.

When alpha is below one-half, recovering a single nearby solution is information-theoretically impossible. The authors instead develop an efficient list-decodable learner that returns a small set of candidates guaranteed to contain a good solution.

When alpha is sufficiently close to one, the algorithm can return a single solution. A rejection-sampling method for noisy location estimation forms another contribution. The abstract provides no empirical results or explicit complexity formulas. The guarantee depends on oblivious independence and the clean-sample fraction, and should not be extended to arbitrary adaptive gradient corruption.

neurips-2023-fluid-mitigating-stragglers.tldr: FLuID assigns smaller adaptive submodels to slow federated clients using invariant dropout.
paragraphs: Federated-learning devices differ in processing speed, so slow clients can determine the duration of a training round. FLuID aims to balance that workload dynamically while maintaining model quality, addressing runtime heterogeneity rather than changing the overall learning objective.

Its Invariant Dropout procedure extracts submodels using a weight-update threshold. Updates from faster clients help identify a tailored submodel for each slower client, informed by performance profiling. The framework adjusts these assignments when runtime conditions change and different devices become stragglers.

Evaluation uses five real-world mobile clients and reports reduced straggler bottlenecks while maintaining baseline model efficiency. The abstract gives no wall-clock speedup or accuracy values. Although federated training keeps raw data local in this setup, the contribution described here is computational load balancing; the abstract does not establish a formal privacy guarantee for the exchanged updates.

neurips-2023-hoh-markerless-multimodal-h.tldr: HOH records markerless human handovers with rich multimodal annotations across 136 objects.
paragraphs: Human-object-human handovers require coordinated grasping, movement, and timing. The HOH dataset captures these interactions without body-tracking markers, aiming to preserve natural behavior while supporting research on handover prediction and eventual human-robot interaction.

It contains 2,720 interactions involving 136 objects and 40 participants, organized into 20 giver-receiver pairs or 40 with role reversal. Data include multiview color and depth, skeletons, fused point clouds, grasp and handedness labels, hand and object segmentations, comfort ratings, object metadata, and aligned three-dimensional models.

The authors train networks for grasp, orientation, and trajectory prediction to demonstrate uses of the resource. The abstract does not provide those models’ numerical performance or claim a deployed robot-handover system. Its primary contribution is the breadth of markerless interaction capture and annotation, with model experiments showing how the data can support several related prediction tasks.

neurips-2023-injecting-multimodal-inform.tldr: BiDock combines protein sequence and structure information with differentiable rigid-pose optimization.
paragraphs: Rigid protein docking predicts a complex from unbound structures without allowing conformational changes. Both sequence-derived coevolutionary information and existing three-dimensional geometry can help, but single-modality methods do not fully combine them. BiDock integrates those information sources within a bilevel optimization framework.

A cross-modal transformer predicts an inter-protein distance map. An inner optimization then selects a rotation and translation that align the rigidly docked pose with that map. The authors differentiate through unrolled gradient descent and use spectral estimation to improve pose initialization.

On challenging antibody-antigen docking, the reported maximum relative improvement over baselines is 234%. The abstract does not specify the corresponding metric or absolute performance, so that number should not be interpreted as a universal accuracy gain. The contribution concerns rigid docking specifically and does not establish equivalent performance when substantial conformational rearrangements are required.

neurips-2023-instructblip-towards-genera.tldr: InstructBLIP tunes a vision-language model to instructions and generalizes across held-out task datasets.
paragraphs: Vision-language systems face diverse tasks and visual inputs, making general-purpose instruction following challenging. This paper studies instruction tuning of pretrained BLIP-2 models using 26 public datasets converted into a common instruction-oriented format.

An instruction-aware Query Transformer extracts visual features suited to the current instruction. The model trains on 13 included datasets and is evaluated zero-shot on the other 13, explicitly testing transfer to held-out task data rather than only measuring training-task performance.

InstructBLIP achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot results on all 13 held-out datasets in the reported comparisons, surpassing BLIP-2 and larger Flamingo models. Individual-task fine-tuning also performs strongly, including 90.7% accuracy on ScienceQA questions with image contexts. The abstract adds qualitative comparisons with contemporary multimodal models. These results demonstrate broad evaluated transfer, while not establishing reliable instruction following for every possible visual task.

neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.tldr: Prompted language models can act as weak learners inside a boosting system for tabular data.
paragraphs: Boosting combines classifiers that perform slightly better than chance into a stronger predictor. This paper investigates whether a prompted language model can supply those weak learners, making it a component of a larger learning algorithm rather than using it only as a standalone few-shot classifier.

Tabular samples are described in text and sampled according to the distribution relevant to the boosting step. The language model summarizes those examples into a classification template. Repeating this process supplies the weak models combined by the boosting procedure.

Experiments show improvements over traditional tree-based boosting in many settings and over few-shot prompting, with occasional advantages over more involved fine-tuning, especially on some small-data tasks. The abstract does not prove that a language model meets the theoretical weak-learning condition for every distribution. Its evidence is that this construction works effectively on the evaluated tabular problems.

neurips-2023-large-language-models-of-co.tldr: Potential bugs in code context sharply reduce completion quality and remain difficult to mitigate.
paragraphs: Code-completion models are often evaluated with clean input code, but real programmers may provide unfinished context containing potential bugs. This paper defines buggy-code completion to study whether models can produce correct programs when that context already contains a harmful pattern.

The authors introduce buggy-HumanEval with synthetic bugs created by meaning-changing operator edits and buggy-FixEval with realistic bugs from user submissions. These datasets separate the effects of controlled changes from problems observed in actual programming attempts.

Potential bugs substantially degrade strong code models. For CODEGEN-2B-MONO, one potential bug in buggy-HumanEval context reduces test-passing rates by more than 50%. Several post-hoc mitigation methods leave a large remaining performance gap. The abstract does not imply every context bug causes failure, but demonstrates that clean-context benchmarks can miss a consequential weakness in practical completion behavior.

neurips-2023-may-the-force-be-with-you-u.tldr: Force-centered pretraining unifies equilibrium and off-equilibrium molecular conformations.
paragraphs: Molecular pretraining often emphasizes equilibrium structures, where local-energy-minimum assumptions support the training objective. Off-equilibrium conformations violate those assumptions yet matter for dynamics. This paper builds a shared force-centered objective covering both types of molecular data.

For off-equilibrium structures, the model learns directly from atomic forces. For equilibrium data, zero-force regularization and force-based denoising approximate nearby forces. The unified model is pretrained on more than 15 million diverse conformations.

The authors report roughly threefold improved force accuracy over an unpretrained Equivariant Transformer. Equilibrium regularization resolves unstable molecular-dynamics simulations observed with the vanilla model, yielding state-of-the-art simulation performance and 2.45x faster inference than NequIP. Property prediction is comparable to state-of-the-art methods. These comparisons concern the evaluated configurations; the abstract does not specify the underlying force-error metric or guarantee stable simulation for every molecular system.
